Header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Danielle Cruz (Redwood SE), Omar Hsu (Redwood Solutions Eng), Raj Patel (StrataHealth - Head of Security), Maya Lopez (IdP Admin), Tom Wu (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): security topics, lots of S S O details, scim provisioning ask, rbac mapping.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): ok everyone thanks for joining, this is lena from redwood, we'll cover SSO SAML and SCIM today and then go into RBAC and audit logs, um try to keep to about 45 minutes for the review and then action items
[01:12] Raj (StrataHealth): thanks lena, appreciate it; quick context we're a healthcare SaaS, we'll be sending PHI to any inference service so compliance and data residency matter a lot for us
[02:05] Maya (IdP Admin): plus we need SCIM to be pretty robust so we can provision groups automatically - we use okta as our idp but we also have ping for a couple of subsidiaries so the idp side is varied
[03:01] Danielle (Redwood SE): great, we typically support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. for okta we have a documented flow and example metadata, and we can also provide a SCIM test harness. for RBAC we recommend a least-privilege role model, mapping groups from SCIM to roles in Redwood
[04:20] Tom (Platform): can you explain the exact attributes you'll accept over SCIM? we map groups in our directory and want to ensure there are no surprises
[05:05] Omar (Redwood): sure, so the default mapping is displayName -> team name, members -> user list, and we support custom attribute mapping if you send extension urns, occasionally the urns are parsed wrong by some idps so we'll give you examples
[06:21] Raj: and for SAML metadata, we need to know if you support multiple assertion consumer urls because we have multiple environments (prod/stage)
[07:05] Lena: yes we do support multiple ACS endpoints, you can upload metadata per environment in the console or we can accept raw metadata xml. we'll include a step-by-step for that.
[08:30] Maya: what about automated de-provisioning? when someone leaves we need them removed quickly to avoid access to PHI
[09:00] Danielle: SCIM de-provisioning is supported, we honour user active attribute changes and group removals. the typical latency is dependent on your provisioning interval - okta lets you set the push frequency - but we process immediate deletes on receipt
[10:15] Raj: audit logs - what granularity do we get? we need admin actions, role changes, token usage, and request traces going to our SIEM
[11:04] Omar: we emit audit logs for user auth events, role changes, token creations, model access events, and admin console actions. logs can be exported to S3 in a customer-owned bucket or we can forward to your SIEM via a secure connector. retention is configurable but by default we retain 90 days in the console and you can request longer retention as an add-on
[12:40] Priya (Compliance): for SOC 2 and ISO, do you provide the full reports or a summary? we need assurance for our auditors and a point of contact
[13:20] Lena: we provide SOC 2 type II report under NDA and an ISO posture summary. i'll send the SOC 2 redaction guide and the contact for our compliance lead.
[14:50] Tom: encryption at rest - do you integrate with our KMS? we need BYOK and HSM-backed keys for certain tenants
[15:30] Danielle: yes we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; in hosted mode we can integrate with cloud KMS providers, and for dedicated or private deployments we can use HSM. there are some differences in key rotation and audit when self-managed keys are used, we'll document those options
[17:00] Raj: data residency - we need data to remain in our region for PHI processing - do you support regional pinning or on-prem?
[17:35] Lena: we have dedicated private deployments and VPC options; for strict residency we'd recommend our Private deployment or a Dedicated cluster in your region, we can keep data on machines in region and provide contractual terms for that
[19:05] Maya: SCIM attribute mapping example would help, and we need an example of the group lifecycle mapping to RBAC roles
[19:40] Omar: we'll share a sample SCIM payload; for RBAC we recommend a minimal set: admin, dev, viewer, and then service roles for automated pipelines. map your Okta groups to these roles and then fine tune with resource-level permissions
[21:10] Raj: what about separation of duties - can we restrict console access so only security can approve role escalations?
[21:45] Danielle: yes, we support role-based console permissions; you can restrict role assignment to a small admin team and create approval workflows - those workflows can be logged in audit logs
[23:12] Tom: on tokens - do we get token-level visibility like who called the API and the model invoked? we need to trace model usage per customer tenant
[24:00] Omar: yes token usage is logged, we break down per-route and per-model metrics and include requester id if available from the token. for multi-tenant we can annotate logs with tenant ids so your SIEM can correlate
[25:45] Maya: when you say 'tenant id' is that scoped to the redwood account or our internal tenant id? we need the attribute to match our internal naming
[26:20] Danielle: we can accept a custom header or encoded claim in the JWT that maps to your internal tenant id, we'll document the claim name to use
[27:50] Raj: any common pitfalls during SAML setup? we've had issues with NameID formats and clock skew
[28:10] Lena: yes clock skew and certificate rollover are the top two; we recommend using EntityID and persistent NameID where possible and ensure your idp and our service have NTP sync. also include all certs in the metadata if you rotate certs often
[29:40] Tom: what about SCIM batching? if we push big group syncs will it throttle?
[30:10] Omar: we have rate limits per tenant for SCIM and a backoff strategy; large initial imports are usually done via a bulk import API or CSV upload, we can support a one-time bootstrap import to avoid throttling during first sync
[31:55] Priya: compliance question - do you sign BAA for PHI?
[32:25] Lena: we can support BAA on Private deployments and some Dedicated arrangements; for hosted accounts we have to evaluate case by case - i'll follow up with legal and include that in the doc pack
[33:40] Maya: for SCIM testing, can you provide a sandbox tenant so we can run the Okta connector before production?
[34:05] Omar: yes we'll stand up a sandbox tenant and provide test credentials, and we'll include a step-by-step Okta app setup guide so you can configure the provisioning connector
[35:30] Raj: are there any limitations on attributes - e.g., custom claims or nested groups?
[36:05] Danielle: nested groups are supported but we flatten them in our mapping by default; for complex group logic we recommend syncing a dedicated group that represents the flattened membership or use a custom attribute that lists resolved members
[37:20] Tom: how do we handle emergency access - break glass scenarios?
[37:55] Danielle: we support temporary elevated roles with TTLs and all elevations are logged; break-glass tokens can be rotated and are limited to certain IP ranges if you want an extra layer
[39:18] Raj: about logs export - do you push to their bucket or we pull? we prefer push to our S3 with SSE-KMS
[40:00] Omar: we can deliver to customer-owned S3 with SSE-KMS; we'll sign a transfer process and set up a secure IAM role for delivery. we can also stream events to a Kinesis or forward to Splunk/Datadog via secure connector
[41:30] Priya: timeline - we'd like to pilot in January and go to production in March, does that align with your onboarding cadence?
[42:05] Lena: that timeline is reasonable; pilot in Jan with a sandbox SCIM integration and then a pilot on dedicated nodes in Feb for residency testing, production by March if legal and BAA are agreed
[43:25] Maya: we also need a clear list of RBAC permissions for reviewers; can you provide a matrix?
[44:00] Danielle: yes i'll produce an RBAC matrix mapping roles to actions and resources, with examples for least-privilege and escalation paths
[45:20] Raj: ok let's recap next steps
[45:35] Lena: recap: redwood sends SSO/SAML metadata example, SCIM sample payload, SOC2/ISO docs, RBAC matrix and we'll schedule the SCIM deep-dive next week. customer provides idp metadata and test account. legal to confirm BAA path.
[46:10] Tom: sounds good, i'll coordinate the idp metadata and share it with lena
[46:40] Priya: i'll loop in our legal for the BAA discussion
[47:00] Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate the detail - this was helpful
[47:20] Lena: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc pack and calendar invites for the deep dive
[48:00] (call ends)
